stemMd: Which part would be a strong candidate to keep in stock under the revised approach?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Only parts that have never been used in any machine.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every costly part regardless of availability.

options.label: C
options.textMd: All former items in exactly their previous quantities.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A readily available substitute that is never needed.

options.label: E
options.textMd: A low-cost part with a long delivery time whose failure stops an important machine.

explanationMd: The revised criteria combine consequence, lead time and substitutability. A cheap but critical, slow-to-replace part fits the case for holding a spare. Neither high price nor past stock status alone decides the issue.

distractorRationale.b: Price alone is no longer the criterion.
distractorRationale.a: Such stock would not address known interruption risks.
distractorRationale.d: The revised approach concerns consequences and practical need.
distractorRationale.c: The manager explicitly did not restore everything.
